Can we host the airflow in local now, mirroring what we have in azure container app. 
Also for the flat file can we have a SFTP or something similar in local docker? [open to ideas here]
[so when we wind down azure, we can keep the job running.]
I'll start by understanding what exists today — the Azure Airflow setup, the harness repo layout, and how flat-file connections work.

# Two env files (split in #209 so app Settings can run extra="forbid"):
#   .env      — infra/compose only: POSTGRES_* (+ VITE_* for the frontend). This is
#               the file compose auto-substitutes ${...} from. setup.sh creates it
#               from .env.example. NOT loaded into the api/worker containers.
#   .env.app  — app config (DATABASE_URL, AZURE_*, AUTH_DEV_BYPASS, SECRET_STORE, …):
#               only keys the app's Settings recognizes. Loaded into api/worker/
#               migrate via env_file below; created from .env.app.example.
# DATABASE_URL is identical across migrate/api/worker. Postgres user/password/db
# carry NO embedded defaults — they come from .env or the shell. The `:?` on the
# canonical postgres block below makes compose fail fast if any is unset, rather
# than baking credentials into the file.
x-database-url: &database-url "REDACTED"

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: "${POSTGRES_USER:?set POSTGRES_USER in .env}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}"
      POSTGRES_DB: "${POSTGRES_DB:?set POSTGRES_DB in .env}"
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  redis:
    # Pinned to 7.x deliberately — Redis 8 bundles the Vector Sets module, which
    # carries an unpatched duplicate-HNSW-ID RCE (see #980 before bumping). Nothing
    # in DataQ uses VSET; 7.x simply does not expose the command surface.
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  # Credential store for the api + worker (ADR 0039), replacing the plaintext
  # RedisSecretStore. Runs in DEV MODE: auto-unsealed, in-memory, KV v2 mounted at
  # secret/ — so restarting it DROPS every stored credential and connections must be
  # re-entered. That is the deliberate dev trade (a persistent vault needs a storage
  # backend and a manual unseal on every boot); production uses a real vault, or
  # Azure Key Vault on the Azure deploy.
  #
  # OpenBao, not HashiCorp Vault: Vault Community has been BUSL-1.1 since 1.15, which
  # CONTRIBUTING rule 40 / ADR 0031 forbid us to DISTRIBUTE. OpenBao is the Linux
  # Foundation fork at the pre-BUSL point, MPL-2.0. The app speaks the KV v2 API, so
  # pointing OPENBAO_ADDR at a real Vault or HCP instead works unchanged.
  #
  # Pinned, not :latest — same rule as the GX and redis:7 pins.
  openbao:
    image: openbao/openbao:2.6.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    # BAO_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID is a CREDENTIAL, so it is never defaulted in this
    # tracked file (CLAUDE.md §11) — scripts/setup.sh generates it into the
    # gitignored .env, exactly as it does the local Postgres password. `:?` fails
    # the stack with this message rather than starting an unreachable vault.
    environment:
      BAO_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID: ${OPENBAO_TOKEN:?run ./scripts/setup.sh (or set OPENBAO_TOKEN) — ADR 0039}
      BAO_DEV_LISTEN_ADDRESS: "0.0.0.0:8200"
    ports:
      # Loopback ONLY — unlike the postgres/redis lines above, this holds the real
      # warehouse credentials a developer entered, behind nothing but a root token
      # sitting in .env on the same machine. Binding it to 0.0.0.0 would expose that
      # to the LAN and invert the point of putting an auth boundary in front of the
      # values (ADR 0039). Matches docker-compose.ghcr.yml.
      - "127.0.0.1:8200:8200"
    cap_add:
      # OpenBao locks its memory so secrets cannot be swapped to disk.
      - IPC_LOCK
    healthcheck:
      # 200 = initialized+unsealed+active. Dev mode unseals itself, but gating on
      # health keeps api/worker from racing the vault on a cold start.
      test: ["CMD", "bao", "status", "-address=http://127.0.0.1:8200"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  # One-shot: applies Alembic migrations then exits 0. api/worker wait on it via
  # service_completed_successfully so `docker compose up` never serves an
  # un-migrated schema (#156). Mirrors setup.sh's `cd backend && alembic ...`
  # because alembic.ini's script_location is relative to backend/.
  migrate:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
    restart: "no"
    command: sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"
    env_file:
      - path: .env.app
        required: false
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: *database-url
    volumes:
      - ./backend:/workspace/backend
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy

  # FastAPI + Celery share one image (backend/Dockerfile, conda env `dataq`).
  # DATABASE_URL / REDIS_URL are overridden here to the in-network service
  # hostnames (the .env defaults point at localhost for host-side dev).
  api:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    env_file:
      - path: .env.app
        required: false
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: *database-url
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
      # Shared across api + worker so a credential the API writes at runtime is
      # readable by connection-driven worker runs (#86) — EnvSecretStore is
      # per-process and cannot do that. NOTE: in openbao mode KV_SECRET_* env vars
      # are NOT consulted (that's `env` mode); set SECRET_STORE=env if you rely on
      # env-provided creds.
      SECRET_STORE: ${SECRET_STORE:-openbao}
      OPENBAO_ADDR: http://openbao:8200
      OPENBAO_TOKEN: ${OPENBAO_TOKEN:?run ./scripts/setup.sh (or set OPENBAO_TOKEN) — ADR 0039}
      # The dev-bypass identity is the workspace admin locally (non-secret dev
      # default; ADR 0027) so /admin + /settings are drivable in dev and E2E.
      # No-colon form: WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS="" in .env opts back OUT (to a
      # non-admin identity, e.g. to exercise the Forbidden gate manually).
      WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS: ${WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS-dev-bypass@dataq.local}
      # Request throttling off in the dev stack (#796): dev-bypass traffic
      # carries no bearer, so a local Playwright run lands in the per-IP
      # unauthenticated class (120/min) and 429s mid-suite. The limiter has its
      # own tests (#725, ADR 0035); set RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true in .env to
      # exercise it manually.
      RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED: ${RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED:-false}
    volumes:
      # Bind-mount source for hot reload; the conda env in the image is untouched.
      - ./backend:/workspace/backend
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      openbao:
        condition: service_healthy
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  worker:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    # -B runs celery-beat embedded in the worker (the #171 orchestration polling
    # schedule). Fine for the single-worker dev stack; prod runs a separate beat.
    command: celery -A backend.app.worker.celery_app worker -B --loglevel=INFO
    env_file:
      - path: .env.app
        required: false
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: *database-url
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
      # Must match the api service so secrets the API writes are visible here (#86).
      SECRET_STORE: ${SECRET_STORE:-openbao}
      OPENBAO_ADDR: http://openbao:8200
      OPENBAO_TOKEN: ${OPENBAO_TOKEN:?run ./scripts/setup.sh (or set OPENBAO_TOKEN) — ADR 0039}
    volumes:
      - ./backend:/workspace/backend
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      openbao:
        condition: service_healthy
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  # React/Vite dev server. corepack pins pnpm from package.json's packageManager.
  # node_modules is an anonymous volume so the host's (possibly macOS-built) copy
  # doesn't clobber the container's. pnpm's ~300MB content-addressable store is
  # relocated to /pnpm-store (OUTSIDE the ./frontend bind) and held in its own
  # volume — so nothing leaks into, or creates an empty mountpoint under, the host
  # working tree. The browser loads from localhost:3000 and the Vite proxy forwards
  # /api + /mcp to the api service over the compose network.
  frontend:
    image: node:24-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    working_dir: /app
    command: sh -c "corepack enable && pnpm config set store-dir /pnpm-store && pnpm install && pnpm dev --host"
    environment:
      VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET: http://api:8000
      # Pass the client-side auth vars into the Vite dev server. Only VITE_*
      # vars are forwarded (DB/secret env stays out of the node container).
      # Substituted from the project .env; dev-bypass defaults on for local dev.
      VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS: ${VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS:-true}
      VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID: ${VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID:-}
      VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID: ${VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID:-}
      VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID: ${VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID:-}
      VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE: ${VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE:-user_impersonation}
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/app
      - /app/node_modules
      - pnpm-store:/pnpm-store
    depends_on:
      - api

  # ─────────────────────────── lineage (opt-in) ────────────────────────────
  # Marquez (Apache-2.0) — the reference `LineageProvider` catalog (ADR 0034, #762):
  # DataQ's OpenLineage emitter (#758) feeds it, and the daily `refresh_lineage_pull`
  # beat task pulls the graph back into the `lineage_edges` cache. TWO extra containers
  # (marquez + its own throwaway Postgres), gated behind the `lineage` **profile** so a
  # plain `docker compose up` never starts them — bring them up explicitly with
  #   docker compose --profile lineage up
  # and point the app at Marquez by setting LINEAGE_PROVIDER=marquez, MARQUEZ_URL=
  # http://marquez:5000, and OPENLINEAGE_URL=http://marquez:5000/api/v1/lineage in
  # .env.app. See docs/orchestration.md for the emit→pull round-trip walkthrough.
  #
  # Marquez's newest release is 0.50.0 (2024-10); its slow cadence is an accepted
  # low risk for a dev-time reference consumer (ADR 0034) — the /api/v1/lineage
  # contract has been stable across releases.
  marquez-db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    profiles: ["lineage"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: marquez
      POSTGRES_DB: marquez
      # trust auth: this is an isolated, network-internal, opt-in dev DB that holds no
      # real data, so no password secures it (no credential is committed — CLAUDE.md).
      POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD: trust
    volumes:
      - marquez_db_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U marquez"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  marquez:
    image: marquezproject/marquez:0.50.0
    profiles: ["lineage"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    # entrypoint waits for the DB, runs Flyway migrations, then serves the API (5000)
    # + admin (5001). No secret: the DB uses trust auth (POSTGRES_PASSWORD is unused).
    environment:
      MARQUEZ_PORT: 5000
      MARQUEZ_ADMIN_PORT: 5001
      POSTGRES_HOST: marquez-db
      POSTGRES_PORT: 5432
      POSTGRES_DB: marquez
      POSTGRES_USER: marquez
      # Unused (marquez-db runs trust auth) — kept only because Marquez's JDBC config
      # requires the var to exist. Ships BLANK per the no-credentials-in-tracked-files
      # rule (CLAUDE.md §11); set MARQUEZ_DB_PASSWORD in .env only if you point this at
      # a real password-auth Postgres.
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${MARQUEZ_DB_PASSWORD:-}"
    ports:
      # Host 5002/5003: macOS binds 5000 (AirPlay Receiver) by default. In-network the
      # app still reaches http://marquez:5000; only host-side browsing uses 5002/5003.
      - "5002:5000"
      - "5003:5001"
    depends_on:
      marquez-db:
        condition: service_healthy

  # ── Local OTLP consumer (opt-in: `docker-compose --profile telemetry up`) ────
  # The non-Azure half of the observability seam (#589/#591). DataQ exports spans
  # AND logs over OTLP/HTTP whenever OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set — App
  # Insights is just one backend behind that seam (ADR 0010), so a local Jaeger
  # gives the same traces with zero Azure. Set in `.env.app`:
  #   OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://jaeger:4318   (compose)
  #   OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 (host dev)
  # UI on http://localhost:16686. Off by default: telemetry costs CPU and most
  # local work doesn't need it — unset endpoint means telemetry is simply off,
  # which is a supported posture, not a degraded one.
  jaeger:
    image: jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.62.0
    profiles: ["telemetry"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED: "true"
    ports:
      - "16686:16686"  # UI
      - "4318:4318"    # OTLP/HTTP receiver (the endpoint DataQ exports to)

volumes:
  postgres_data:
  pnpm-store:
  marquez_db_data:

===REGISTRY===
"""Connection-type → adapter + runner registry.

The single place that maps a ``Connection.type`` to its `ConnectionAdapter`
(`get_connection_adapter`, all six types) and — for datasources only — to its
`CheckRunner` builder (`build_check_runner`). Service/worker code dispatches
through these and never branches on ``connection.type`` itself; adding a
datasource is an entry here plus the adapter/runner, nothing else.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Callable, Generator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any, Protocol

from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
from backend.app.core.secrets import SecretStore
from backend.app.datasources.adls import AdlsConnectionAdapter
from backend.app.datasources.base import (
    BatchSpec,
    CheckRunner,
    ConnectionAdapter,
    ExpiringCredentialAdapter,
    ResolvedTarget,
    TargetShapeError,
)
from backend.app.datasources.flatfile import build_flatfile_runner
from backend.app.datasources.iceberg import IcebergConnectionAdapter, build_iceberg_runner
from backend.app.datasources.s3 import S3ConnectionAdapter
from backend.app.datasources.snowflake import SnowflakeConnectionAdapter, build_snowflake_runner
from backend.app.datasources.unity_catalog import (
    UnityCatalogConnectionAdapter,
    build_unity_catalog_runner,
)
from backend.app.orchestration.adf import ADFConnectionAdapter
from backend.app.orchestration.airflow import AirflowConnectionAdapter
from backend.app.orchestration.dbt import DbtConnectionAdapter

log = get_logger(__name__)


class UnsupportedConnectionTypeError(ValueError):
    """Raised when no adapter is registered for a connection type."""


# Datasource and orchestration-provider connection types share this one registry
# (both implement the `ConnectionAdapter` seam); the run path keeps them apart —
# only datasources get a `CheckRunner`. ADF, Airflow, and dbt are orchestration
# providers, so their adapters live under `orchestration/`, not `datasources/`
# (CLAUDE.md §4).
_ADAPTERS: dict[str, ConnectionAdapter] = {
    "snowflake": SnowflakeConnectionAdapter(),
    "adls_gen2": AdlsConnectionAdapter(),
    "s3": S3ConnectionAdapter(),
    "unity_catalog": UnityCatalogConnectionAdapter(),
    "iceberg": IcebergConnectionAdapter(),
    "adf": ADFConnectionAdapter(),
    "airflow": AirflowConnectionAdapter(),
    "dbt": DbtConnectionAdapter(),
}


def get_connection_adapter(conn_type: str) -> ConnectionAdapter:
    adapter = _ADAPTERS.get(conn_type)
    if adapter is None:
        raise UnsupportedConnectionTypeError(
            f"No connection adapter registered for type {conn_type!r}"
        )
    return adapter


def credential_expiry(
    conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], secret: str, **extra_secrets: Any
) -> datetime | None:
    """When this connection's credential stops working (#838), or ``None``.

    The one place that asks an adapter about credential lifetime, so callers never
    branch on `connection.type`. ``None`` means **unknown** — the adapter doesn't
    implement `ExpiringCredentialAdapter`, the credential carries no expiry, or the
    read failed. It never means "does not expire".

    Fail-soft by construction: a credential lifetime is an advisory signal, so a
    surprising credential shape — or an unregistered type — must not break the
    caller (connection CRUD, the daily sweep). The failure is logged with the
    connection **type** but **without the secret and without the exception text**:
    a malformed credential's error can quote the credential itself (the #536
    precedent), while the type is a non-secret identifier and the only thing that
    makes the line actionable.
    """
    try:
        adapter = get_connection_adapter(conn_type)
        if not isinstance(adapter, ExpiringCredentialAdapter):
            return None
        return adapter.credential_expiry(config, secret, **extra_secrets)
    except Exception:
        log.warning("credential_expiry_unreadable", type=conn_type)
        return None


# ───────────────────────── CheckRunner registry ─────────────────────
#
# Only datasources get a runner (orchestration providers are absent → asking for
# their runner raises). Each builder is normalised to one signature so the worker
# can dispatch through `build_check_runner` without branching on the type. The
# underlying `build_*` take primitives (not the ORM `Connection`) to keep the
# adapters decoupled from `db/`; the caller unpacks the row.


class _RunnerBuilder(Protocol):
    def __call__(
        self,
        *,
        conn_type: str,
        config: dict[str, Any],
        secret_ref: str | None,
        secret_store: SecretStore,
        catalog: str | None,
    ) -> CheckRunner: ...

# Harness Airflow image — apache/airflow + key-based client libs + the DAGs baked in.
# Once built+pushed to the registry, set Terraform's `airflow_image` to this
# (replacing the public apache/airflow default) so the Airflow Container App ships the DAGs.
#
# Build (from harness root, so the context can see airflow/):
#   docker build -f airflow/Dockerfile -t airflow-dataq:latest .

FROM apache/airflow:2.10.5

COPY airflow/requirements.txt /tmp/harness-requirements.txt
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /tmp/harness-requirements.txt

COPY airflow/dags/ /opt/airflow/dags/

# Webserver auth: Azure AD (Entra) OAuth SSO with app-role → Airflow-role mapping.
# Reads the OAuth client id/secret/tenant from the container env at runtime.
COPY airflow/webserver_config.py /opt/airflow/webserver_config.py

===AIRFLOW README===
# DataQ harness — Airflow (§3 load + trigger)

The **Clock-2** orchestrator (load + trigger), hosted on Container Apps (see
`terraform/airflow.tf`). DAGs read files the §2a Jobs drop in the ADLS landing zone,
load them into Snowflake / Unity Catalog, and on success POST DataQ's webhook → DataQ
records the `pipeline_run` and fires the bound suite.

**All auth key-based** (disposable-harness decision): ADLS via the storage connection
string, Snowflake via user/password, Databricks via PAT.

## Image

`Dockerfile` = `apache/airflow:2.10.5` + `requirements.txt` client libs + `dags/`.

```bash
docker build -f airflow/Dockerfile -t airflow-dataq:latest .   # from harness root
# verify DAGs parse (no metadata DB needed):
docker run --rm --entrypoint python -e PYTHONPATH=/opt/airflow/dags airflow-dataq:latest \
  -c "from airflow.models.dagbag import DagBag; b=DagBag('/opt/airflow/dags', include_examples=False); print(b.import_errors or 'OK', sorted(b.dags))"
```

| DAG | Flow | Trigger | Loads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flow_a_snowflake_load` | A | schedule `30 1 * * *` | ADLS → Snowflake (orders/lines/payments/refunds/returns/customers/products) |

The event-driven Flow A (orders → Snowflake on storage-event) is **ADF**, not Airflow —

"""ADLS Gen2 (Azure Data Lake Storage) connection adapter.

A flat-file datasource (CLAUDE.md §4): DQ checks run against files in a
container. Week 2 ships only the `ConnectionAdapter` seam (config validation +
connectivity `test`); the GX pandas/ABFS `CheckRunner` that reads the files is a
Week-3 concern.

**Auth — v1 supports SAS only.** The roadmap lists managed-identity *and* SAS,
but managed identity has no stored secret and is only meaningfully testable once
DataQ runs on Azure with an ambient identity — so it (and the broader
``connections.secret_ref`` nullability change) is deferred to Week 7. A
``managed_identity`` config is accepted by the schema but rejected with a clear
message in v1; use a SAS token (held in the SecretStore).

``test`` builds a ``BlobServiceClient`` from the account URL + SAS and reads the
container's properties — a green test means the endpoint is reachable, the SAS
authenticates, and the container exists. The Azure SDK is imported lazily (per
``core/secrets.py``) so non-ADLS deployments don't pay the import cost; like the
other adapters it runs live and fails-soft pending real credentials.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, field_validator, model_validator

from backend.app.core.credential_expiry import azure_sas_expiry

# Fail fast rather than hang the request thread on an unreachable account.
_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10


class AdlsConfig(BaseModel):
    """Non-secret ADLS Gen2 connection config (the SAS token comes from secrets).

    Maps from ``Connection.config``. ``account_url`` is the storage endpoint
    (e.g. ``https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net``); ``container`` is the
    filesystem. The SAS token is resolved from the SecretStore at test time.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    account_url: str
    container: str
    auth_type: Literal["sas", "managed_identity"] = "sas"

    @field_validator("account_url")
    @classmethod
    def _http_url(cls, value: str) -> str:
        if not value.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
            raise ValueError("account_url must start with http:// or https://")
        return value.rstrip("/")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _managed_identity_deferred(self) -> AdlsConfig:
        if self.auth_type == "managed_identity":
            raise ValueError(
                "managed_identity auth is deferred to Week 7 (needs an ambient Azure "
                "identity to test against); use auth_type='sas' with a SAS token in v1"
            )
        return self


class AdlsConnectionAdapter:
    """`ConnectionAdapter` for ADLS Gen2 — config validation + a container probe."""

    def validate_config(self, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> AdlsConfig:
        return AdlsConfig.model_validate(raw)

    def credential_expiry(self, raw: dict[str, Any], secret: str, **_: Any) -> datetime | None:
        """When this connection's SAS stops working (#838), or ``None``.

        The credential IS the expiry notice — a SAS prints `se=` in its own text —
        so this is a read, not an estimate. It is exactly this connection type
        whose silent expiry left prod lineage dark for six days (#828).
        """
        return azure_sas_expiry(secret)

    def test(self, raw: dict[str, Any], secret: str, **_: Any) -> None:
        """Read the container's properties via SAS; raise on any failure.

        ``secret`` is the SAS token. Retries are disabled so an auth/endpoint
        failure surfaces immediately rather than after the SDK's retry budget.
        """
        from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient

        config = self.validate_config(raw)
        # The azure-storage-blob surface is only partially typed (e.g. close() is
        # unannotated); treat the client as dynamic so strict mypy doesn't flag
        # no-untyped-call on the SDK methods.
        client: Any = BlobServiceClient(
            account_url=config.account_url,
            credential=secret,
            retry_total=0,
            connection_timeout=_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            read_timeout=_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
        )
        try:
            client.get_container_client(config.container).get_container_properties()
        finally:
            client.close()

Two responsibilities for the flat-file datasources, both behind the same
primitives the SQL adapters use (raw config dict + resolved secret, never the ORM
row — keeps `datasources/` decoupled from `db/`):

* **IO** — `download_bytes` fetches a whole object/blob and `read_dataframe`
  parses it into pandas; `RangeReader` + `read_range` serve the cases that need
  only *part* of it. Shared by the column profiler (service layer) and the runner.

  Which one a caller reaches for is a real decision, not a preference: running
  checks needs every row and column, but a schema read or a row count does not,
  and paying full egress plus worker memory for either on a scheduled path is the
  #854 shape (#882/#942). Parquet answers both from its footer — a couple of
  small range GETs whatever the object's size — and a CSV takes a bounded head
  read for its schema and a streamed scan for its count.
* **Runner** — `FlatFileCheckRunner` runs GX expectations against the file by
  loading it into an in-memory pandas DataFrame and handing that to GX's pandas
  datasource, then mapping the result via the shared `gx_runner` machinery. The
  `CheckRunner` interface is table-shaped; for a flat-file datasource the
  ``table`` argument carries the **file path** and ``schema`` is unused.

the run path is fully testable with a canned frame; only the network download is
the deferred-smoke seam.

    )


def _blob_service(acfg: AdlsConfig, secret: str) -> Any:
    """An ADLS `BlobServiceClient` for `acfg` (caller must `.close()` it)."""
    from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient

    return BlobServiceClient(account_url=acfg.account_url, credential=secret)


def download_bytes(*, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], path: str, secret: str) -> bytes:
    """Fetch the object/blob bytes from S3 or ADLS Gen2 (live seam).

    Takes the connection's `type` + raw `config` + resolved `secret` (the caller
    owns the SecretStore), so this module never touches the DB.
    """
    if conn_type == "s3":
        cfg = S3Config.model_validate(config)
        body: bytes = _s3_client(cfg, secret).get_object(Bucket=cfg.bucket, Key=path)["Body"].read()
        return body

    acfg = AdlsConfig.model_validate(config)
    client_az = _blob_service(acfg, secret)
    try:
        blob = client_az.get_blob_client(container=acfg.container, blob=path)
        downloaded: bytes = blob.download_blob().readall()
        return downloaded
    finally:
        client_az.close()


def object_size(*, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], path: str, secret: str) -> int:
    """Byte length of exactly ``path`` — one metadata call (live seam, #882)."""
    if conn_type == "s3":
        cfg = S3Config.model_validate(config)
        length: int = _s3_client(cfg, secret).head_object(Bucket=cfg.bucket, Key=path)[
            "ContentLength"
        ]
        return length

    acfg = AdlsConfig.model_validate(config)
    client_az = _blob_service(acfg, secret)
    try:
        blob = client_az.get_blob_client(container=acfg.container, blob=path)
        size: int = blob.get_blob_properties().size
        return size
    finally:
        client_az.close()


def read_range(
    *, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], path: str, secret: str, start: int, length: int
) -> bytes:
    """``length`` bytes of ``path`` from offset ``start`` (live seam, #882).

    Both stores serve HTTP range requests; this is the primitive that lets a
    Parquet footer or a CSV header be read without paying for the whole object.

    A range that *starts* in bounds and *ends* past EOF is served short by both
    stores, so asking for more than exists is safe. A range whose **start** is at
    or past EOF is not: S3 answers 416 and Azure raises `InvalidRange`. That is
    reachable — `RangeReader` snapshots the size once, so an object truncated by a
    producer mid-read can push a later request past the new end. It surfaces as a
    classified read failure at every call site rather than a wrong answer, which
    is the right outcome; it is called out here so nobody plans around a
    short-read that will not happen.
    """
    if length <= 0:
        return b""
    if conn_type == "s3":
        cfg = S3Config.model_validate(config)
        # Inclusive end, per RFC 7233 — `bytes=0-1023` is the first 1024 bytes.
        body: bytes = (
            _s3_client(cfg, secret)
            .get_object(Bucket=cfg.bucket, Key=path, Range=f"bytes={start}-{start + length - 1}")[
                "Body"
            ]
            .read()
        )
        return body

    acfg = AdlsConfig.model_validate(config)
    client_az = _blob_service(acfg, secret)
    try:
        blob = client_az.get_blob_client(container=acfg.container, blob=path)
        downloaded: bytes = blob.download_blob(offset=start, length=length).readall()
        return downloaded
    finally:
        client_az.close()

def iter_files(
    *, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], prefix: str, secret: str
) -> Generator[FileRef]:
    """Stream objects/blobs under `prefix` on a flat-file datasource (live seam).

    A generator, so a caller that only needs a running maximum never holds the
    whole listing (#943). The ADLS client is released in a ``finally``, which runs
    on exhaustion **and** on ``close()`` — so a caller that abandons the iterator
    early must close it (`resolve_batch_file` does, via `contextlib.closing`)
    rather than leave the connection pool to the garbage collector.
    """
    if conn_type == "s3":
        cfg = S3Config.model_validate(config)
        paginator = _s3_client(cfg, secret).get_paginator("list_objects_v2")
        for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket=cfg.bucket, Prefix=prefix):
            for obj in page.get("Contents", []):
                yield FileRef(path=obj["Key"], last_modified=obj.get("LastModified"))
        return

    acfg = AdlsConfig.model_validate(config)
    client_az = _blob_service(acfg, secret)
    try:
        container = client_az.get_container_client(acfg.container)
        for blob in container.list_blobs(name_starts_with=prefix):
            yield FileRef(path=blob.name, last_modified=getattr(blob, "last_modified", None))
    finally:
        client_az.close()


def list_files(
    *, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], prefix: str, secret: str
) -> list[FileRef]:
    """The whole listing under `prefix` as a list (live seam).

    Kept for callers that genuinely want every entry; batch resolution does not,
    and uses `iter_files` instead (#943).
    """
    return list(iter_files(conn_type=conn_type, config=config, prefix=prefix, secret=secret))

content.text: I have what I need to shape this. Let me confirm four scoping decisions before writing the plan.

questions.question: For the local flat-file store, which backend should replace ADLS?

options.label: Azurite (zero DataQ change)
options.description: DataQ's adls_gen2 path is 100% Blob API (BlobServiceClient / get_blob_client / list_blobs / ranged downloads) — Azurite (MIT, Microsoft) serves all of it, so the SAME connection type, adapter, runner and existing checks keep working untouched. Cost lands entirely on the harness writers (mockdata AdlsStore + DAG _harness.py use the DFS/DataLake API, which Azurite does NOT serve — each needs a ~30-line blob variant).
options.preview:
DataQ code changes:  0
Harness changes:     mockdata/storage.py AdlsStore -> blob API
                     airflow/dags/_harness.py  -> blob API
Connection config:   account_url=http://azurite:10000/devstoreaccount1
                     auth_type=sas, container=landing

options.label: MinIO/S3 + endpoint_url feature
options.description: Add an optional `endpoint_url` to S3Config and pass it through `_s3_client` + `S3ConnectionAdapter.test` (~15 lines, one call site each) — this is a genuine product feature: it unlocks MinIO, Ceph, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, Backblaze for real customers, not just local dev. Licensing caveat: MinIO server is AGPL-3.0, so it can sit in the untracked harness compose but NOT in DataQ's docker-compose.yml under rule 40; SeaweedFS/s3proxy (Apache-2.0) are the compliant substitutes.
options.preview:
DataQ code changes:  S3Config.endpoint_url + _s3_client + test()
Harness changes:     mockdata S3Store, DAG s3 reader
Bonus:               real feature - any S3-compatible store
License watch:       MinIO = AGPL-3.0 (rule 40 / ADR 0031)

options.label: New SFTP datasource type
options.description: A real enterprise flat-file source (bank/retail EDI drops) and SFTP supports ranged reads so the #882 range machinery works. But it is a new connection TYPE: it touches 12 backend files and 8 frontend files (registry, check_service, run_target, dataset_reader, profile_service, schema_drift, asset_identity, secret_names, mcp/server, models, custom_sql, flatfile + connections.ts, connectionFormSpec, connectionSources, connectionVisuals, namespaceLabel, suiteTarget, Assets.tsx, ComparisonCheckForm) plus an ADR, docs and the feature matrix. Days of work, and it does not mirror what Azure runs today.
options.preview:
Backend registration points:  12 files
Frontend registration points:  8 files
Also needs: ADR, docs, feature-matrix, tests, UI spec
Mirrors current Azure setup: no

options.label: Azurite now + S3 endpoint as a feature
options.description: Do the like-for-like swap with Azurite (zero DataQ change, existing checks and suites unchanged) so the wind-down is low-risk, and separately file the S3 endpoint_url work as a product feature issue on its own merits. SFTP stays a separate post-v1 product decision with its own ADR.
options.preview:
Now:   Azurite -> adls_gen2 keeps working as-is
Issue: S3 endpoint_url (S3-compatible stores)
Issue: SFTP datasource type (ADR + 20 files)
Risk:  lowest - no change to the tested run path

questions.question: How offline does the end state need to be once Azure is gone?

options.label: Airflow + files local; keep SaaS
options.description: Snowflake and Databricks are NOT Azure, so they survive an Azure wind-down as long as those accounts live. The DAGs keep loading into them; only the landing zone moves local. Smallest change, but the flows die again when Snowflake lapses (~2026-08-25 per the current plan).

options.label: Fully offline, via local Iceberg
options.description: Also give the table-shaped flows a local target. DataQ already HAS a fully-local table datasource: native pyiceberg (ADR 0030) works against a filesystem warehouse + SQLite catalog with zero cloud — Flow D's iceberg-writer is the existing precedent. Local Airflow would write Iceberg instead of Snowflake/UC, so the stack survives Snowflake and Databricks lapsing too.

options.label: Both, staged
options.description: Land local Airflow + local files first (unblocks the Azure wind-down), then add the local-Iceberg targets as a follow-up before Snowflake lapses. Sequenced so nothing is a big-bang.

questions.question: Where should the local stack live?

options.label: Harness repo (ADR 0021)
options.description: ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/local/docker-compose.yml. The DAGs, mockdata generator and image definitions already live there and are deliberately not git-tracked. Keeps harness content out of the shipped product and matches ADR 0021. DataQ's repo gets docs only.

options.label: DataQ repo compose profile
options.description: A `docker compose --profile orchestration up` service set in DataQ's own docker-compose.yml, mirroring how the Marquez (lineage) and Jaeger (telemetry) opt-in profiles already work. Makes a local Airflow available to any DataQ contributor and to E2E, but pulls harness DAGs into the shipped repo.

options.label: Split: engine in DataQ, DAGs in harness
options.description: Airflow engine services as an opt-in profile in DataQ's compose (contributor value, mirrors marquez/jaeger), with the DAG folder bind-mounted from the harness repo via a path env var. Product repo stays free of harness data content.

questions.question: ADF has no local equivalent — how should we handle losing it?

options.label: Accept the loss, document it
options.description: ADF is Azure-only SaaS with no emulator. When Azure winds down, the ADF provider keeps its code, tests and docs but loses live coverage; Flow A's ADF pipelines and their bound suites stop. Record it in the feature matrix and ops log as a known coverage gap rather than pretending otherwise.

options.label: Keep a minimal Azure ADF footprint
options.description: Wind down everything else but leave the ADF factory + its two pipelines alive (ADF bills per activity-run, so an idle factory is near-zero) so the third orchestration provider keeps real live coverage. Costs a small residual Azure surface and an Azure identity to keep working.

options.label: Synthesize ADF events locally
options.description: Replay recorded Azure Monitor common-alert-schema payloads against the local /api/v1/orchestration/events/adf receiver. Exercises the ingest path end-to-end with no Azure, but the ADF REST polling fallback stays uncovered — a partial, honest-about-it substitute.

    """Read ``<artifacts_uri>/<job>/<relpath>``; None if absent.

    ``relpath`` selects the per-job artifact — ``latest/run_results.json`` (the
    poll default) or ``latest/manifest.json`` (lineage, #759). Dispatches on the
    ``artifacts_uri`` scheme. Cloud SDKs are imported lazily (per
    ``core/secrets.py``) so the module — and its unit tests, which patch this
    function — never require azure/boto3. Transport/auth errors propagate (the poll
    task fails soft per connection).

    parsed = urlparse(config.artifacts_uri)
    scheme = parsed.scheme

    if scheme == "file":
        from pathlib import Path

        path = Path(parsed.path) / job / relpath
        return path.read_bytes() if path.exists() else None

    if scheme == "adls":
        from azure.core.exceptions import ResourceNotFoundError
        from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient

        account = parsed.netloc
        container, _, prefix = parsed.path.lstrip("/").partition("/")
        blob = f"{prefix}/{job}/{relpath}" if prefix else f"{job}/{relpath}"
        # Bound socket connect/read like the ADLS datasource adapter — `test()` runs
        # this synchronously in the request thread, so an unreachable account must
        # fail fast, not hang. (`download_blob(timeout=)` is only the server-side op
        # timeout, so set the client-level socket timeouts too.)
        client = BlobServiceClient(
            account_url=f"https://{account}.blob.core.windows.net",
            credential=secret,
            connection_timeout=int(_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS),
            read_timeout=int(_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS),
        )
        try:
            blob_bytes: bytes = (
                client.get_blob_client(container, blob)
                .download_blob(timeout=int(_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS))
                .readall()
            )
            return blob_bytes
        except ResourceNotFoundError:
            return None

    # s3
    import boto3
    from botocore.config import Config
    from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

    bucket = parsed.netloc
    prefix = parsed.path.lstrip("/")
    key = f"{prefix}/{job}/{relpath}" if prefix else f"{job}/{relpath}"
    client = boto3.client(
        "s3",
        region_name=config.region,
        aws_access_key_id=config.access_key_id,
        aws_secret_access_key=secret,
        # Bound connect/read like the S3 datasource adapter — `test()` runs this in
        # the request thread; boto3's ~60s defaults would hang on a blackholed host.
        config=Config(
            connect_timeout=int(_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS), read_timeout=int(_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
        ),
    )
    try:
        data: bytes = client.get_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=key)["Body"].read()
        return data
    except ClientError as exc:
        if exc.response.get("Error", {}).get("Code") in ("NoSuchKey", "404"):
            return None
        raise

# Local Airflow + local flat-file store — an Azure-free alternative, kept ready

## Context

Azure is **not** being wound down. This is a readiness exercise: stand up and *prove*
an Azure-free equivalent of the harness so that if/when the wind-down happens, the
flows keep running rather than needing a design under time pressure. Both stacks
coexist; nothing in Azure is torn down or reconfigured.

Today the live-run evidence for DataQ's flat-file and Airflow paths comes entirely from
Azure: the ADLS landing zone (`mockdata` Jobs → `landing/`) and Airflow on Container
Apps (`terraform/airflow.tf`, CeleryExecutor + Postgres + Redis). Lose the subscription
and both go dark at once.

Decisions taken (see the four scoping answers):

- **Flat file → MinIO / S3-compatible**, which needs one genuine DataQ feature: an
  optional `endpoint_url` on the S3 connection. That is worth shipping on its own
  merits — it unlocks MinIO, Ceph, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi and Backblaze for real users,
  not just local dev.
- **Staged offline**: local Airflow + local files first; local Iceberg targets after,
  so the stack also survives Snowflake/Databricks lapsing.
- **Local stack lives in the harness repo** (`~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/`, untracked,
  ADR 0021). The DataQ repo gets the `endpoint_url` feature plus docs, nothing else.
- **ADF: accept the loss, document it.** ADF is Azure-only SaaS with no emulator. This
  is recorded now as a contingency, not an action.

### What made this cheap to verify

- Every S3 read in the run path goes through **one** client factory,
  [flatfile.py:151](backend/app/datasources/flatfile.py#L151) `_s3_client` — used by
  `download_bytes`, `object_size`, `read_range`, `iter_files` and the schema/count
  reads. One change covers all of them.
- `IcebergConfig.properties` is **freeform pass-through** into `load_catalog`
  ([iceberg.py:138](backend/app/datasources/iceberg.py#L138) `catalog_properties`), and a
  credential-less local catalog is already supported — so Part 3 needs **zero** DataQ
  code.

### Licensing (rule 40 / ADR 0031)

MinIO server is **AGPL-3.0**. It goes **only** into the untracked harness compose, which
DataQ does not distribute. It must **not** be added to DataQ's `docker-compose.yml`
(where OpenBao/Marquez/Jaeger were each license-checked). If a tracked local S3 is ever
wanted, use **SeaweedFS** or **s3proxy** (both Apache-2.0) — the `endpoint_url` feature
works with either.

---

## Part 0 — DataQ: S3-compatible endpoints (the only product change)

One functionality: *"the S3 connection can address a non-AWS, S3-compatible endpoint."*

**`backend/app/datasources/s3.py`** — `S3Config` gains:
- `endpoint_url: str | None` — validated `http(s)://` and right-stripped, mirroring
  `AdlsConfig._http_url` in [adls.py](backend/app/datasources/adls.py).
- `addressing_style: Literal["auto", "path", "virtual"] = "auto"` — `auto` resolves to
  **path** when `endpoint_url` is set, and to boto3's default otherwise. This is not
  optional polish: MinIO and SeaweedFS reject virtual-host addressing, so without it
  boto3 resolves `bucket.minio:9000` and every read fails.
- `S3ConnectionAdapter.test` passes both into `boto3.client` alongside the existing
  fail-fast `Config`.

**`backend/app/datasources/flatfile.py`** — `_s3_client` takes the same two fields from
the config it already receives. No call-site changes; all five read paths inherit it.

**`backend/app/orchestration/dbt.py`** — `DbtConfig` + the `s3` branch of `_read_artifact`
get the same two fields. Same seam, and skipping it would leave the dbt artifact poller
as the one S3 path that cannot reach a local store — the kind of quiet divergence between
two clients this codebase avoids.

**Frontend** — add the two optional fields to the `s3` entry in
[connectionFormSpec.ts:91](frontend/src/components/connections/connectionFormSpec.ts#L91),
following the existing optional-field pattern. No new connection type, so the ~20
type-registration points (`check_service`, `run_target`, `dataset_reader`,
`profile_service`, `schema_drift`, `asset_identity`, `connections.ts`, …) are untouched.

**Security note for the PR:** an operator-supplied endpoint is a fetch target
(SSRF-shaped). This matches the existing posture for `adls_gen2.account_url` and
`iceberg.catalog_uri` — connection configs are admin-authored — and the scheme is
validated. Call it out explicitly in the PR rather than letting it pass unexamined.

**Tests** (`backend/tests/datasources/test_s3.py`, `test_flatfile.py`, dbt tests):
config validation incl. `auto → path` inference and scheme rejection; assert the boto3
kwargs actually carry `endpoint_url` and `s3={"addressing_style": ...}`. Per the
standing habit, **mutation-check each new regression test** — revert the fix and confirm
it fails for the right reason.

---

## Part 1 — Harness: local Airflow mirroring Container Apps

`~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/local/docker-compose.yml`, same topology as
`terraform/airflow.tf`: postgres (metadata) · redis (broker) · `airflow-init` (db migrate
+ admin user) · scheduler · webserver · celery worker — all from the **existing**
`airflow/Dockerfile` (`apache/airflow:2.10.5` + DAGs + client libs), CeleryExecutor,
reusing the env var names from `local.airflow_env` verbatim
(`EXECUTE_TASKS_NEW_PYTHON_INTERPRETER`, `LOAD_EXAMPLES=False`,
`API__AUTH_BACKENDS=basic_auth,session`).

**One blocker to fix in the image:** `airflow/webserver_config.py` reads
`os.environ["AZURE_OAUTH_TENANT_ID"]` at import and hard-`KeyError`s without Entra vars —
and the init container imports it too. Make it fall back to `AUTH_DB` when the OAuth env
is absent, so **one image** serves both ACA (Entra SSO) and local (basic auth). The REST
basic-auth path DataQ polls stays identical either way.

**MinIO** service + an `mc` bootstrap container creating the `landing` bucket and an
access key.

**Networking:** declare DataQ's compose network as `external` so DataQ's api/worker reach
`http://airflow-webserver:8080` and the DAG callback reaches
`http://api:8000/api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow`. The DataQ Airflow connection's
`base_url` **must equal** `DATAQ_AIRFLOW_BASE_URL` — run attribution depends on it.

**`local/harness_local.sh`** — the `scripts/harness_window.sh` analogue:
`up | seed | run [--dags] | down`, driving the same DAG list over the Airflow REST API.

---

## Part 2 — Harness writers move to S3

- **`mockdata/storage.py`** — add `S3Store` beside `LocalStore`/`AdlsStore` and teach
  `make_store` the `s3://<bucket>/<prefix>` scheme. ~30 lines, mirrors `AdlsStore`.
- **`airflow/dags/_harness.py`** — `_adls_filesystem` / `count_feed_files` / `read_feed`
  are DataLake-only; add an S3 path selected by env so the **same DAG files** run in both
  places, unedited.
- **Event modality (bonus of choosing S3):** MinIO bucket notifications can POST to a
  webhook on `s3:ObjectCreated`. Reuse the `eventgrid_receiver/` shape to translate that
  into `POST /api/v1/dags/flow_a_payments_event/dagRuns`, preserving the event-driven
  Airflow row of the orchestration matrix locally. Azurite has no equivalent.

---

## Part 3 — Staged: local Iceberg targets (no DataQ code)

Verified above: `catalog_type=sql` + a SQLite catalog URI + a local or MinIO warehouse
(`properties={"s3.endpoint": ...}`) already works, credential-less. Add DAG variants that
write Iceberg instead of Snowflake/UC so the stack survives those accounts lapsing. Flow
D's `iceberg-writer` is the working precedent. Sequenced after Parts 0–2 land and are
proven.

---

## Part 4 — Docs

- `docs/datasources-checks.md` + `docs/feature-matrix.md` — S3-compatible endpoints.
- `docs/ops-log.md` — the readiness exercise, and the ADF contingency: Azure-only SaaS,
  no emulator, so on a real wind-down the provider keeps its code/tests/docs but loses
  live coverage. Recorded, not actioned.
- Harness `README.md` — the local section + the MinIO/AGPL boundary.

No new ADR: ADR 0021 already covers the harness, and `endpoint_url` is a config
extension, not an architecture decision.

---

## Verification

**Gate before push** (local, not CI-first): Black · Ruff · mypy · **Bandit** · pytest with
the `--cov-fail-under=80` gate · frontend lint/test. Then `/code-review` agents on the PR.

**Live proof — the point of the exercise.** Fixtures cannot settle this: MinIO is a
different server implementation from AWS, and `LastModified` / `head_object` /
`list_objects_v2` cross a driver boundary. Only a live run is evidence (the UC-freshness
and Parquet-freshness lesson).

1. Bring up the local stack; seed via `mockdata` → MinIO.
2. Create a DataQ `s3` connection with `endpoint_url` pointing at MinIO → **Test** green.
3. Run the flat-file suite → rows read; run **volume** and **arrival-time freshness**
   monitors and confirm real readings off MinIO's `LastModified`.
4. Trigger a DAG over the Airflow REST API; confirm DataQ records the `pipeline_run`
   **both** via 10-min polling **and** via the HMAC callback, and that a bound suite fires.
5. Confirm the dbt artifact poller reads `run_results.json` from MinIO.
6. Re-run the same S3 checks against real AWS (or the existing suites) to prove the
   `auto` addressing default did not regress the AWS path.

**PRs:** (1) S3-compatible endpoints + tests, (2) docs. The harness is untracked — no PR.

  reads. One change covers all of them.
- `IcebergConfig.properties` is **freeform pass-through** into `load_catalog`
  ([iceberg.py:138](backend/app/datasources/iceberg.py#L138) `catalog_properties`), and a
  credential-less local catalog is already supported — so Part 3 needs **zero** DataQ
  code.

### Licensing (rule 40 / ADR 0031)

MinIO server is **AGPL-3.0**. It goes **only** into the untracked harness compose, which
DataQ does not distribute. It must **not** be added to DataQ's `docker-compose.yml`
(where OpenBao/Marquez/Jaeger were each license-checked). If a tracked local S3 is ever
wanted, use **SeaweedFS** or **s3proxy** (both Apache-2.0) — the `endpoint_url` feature
works with either.

---

## Part 0 — DataQ: S3-compatible endpoints (the only product change)

One functionality: *"the S3 connection can address a non-AWS, S3-compatible endpoint."*

**`backend/app/datasources/s3.py`** — `S3Config` gains:
- `endpoint_url: str | None` — validated `http(s)://` and right-stripped, mirroring
  `AdlsConfig._http_url` in [adls.py](backend/app/datasources/adls.py).
- `addressing_style: Literal["auto", "path", "virtual"] = "auto"` — `auto` resolves to
  **path** when `endpoint_url` is set, and to boto3's default otherwise. This is not
  optional polish: MinIO and SeaweedFS reject virtual-host addressing, so without it
  boto3 resolves `bucket.minio:9000` and every read fails.
- `S3ConnectionAdapter.test` passes both into `boto3.client` alongside the existing
  fail-fast `Config`.

**`backend/app/datasources/flatfile.py`** — `_s3_client` takes the same two fields from
the config it already receives. No call-site changes; all five read paths inherit it.

**`backend/app/orchestration/dbt.py`** — `DbtConfig` + the `s3` branch of `_read_artifact`
get the same two fields. Same seam, and skipping it would leave the dbt artifact poller
as the one S3 path that cannot reach a local store — the kind of quiet divergence between
two clients this codebase avoids.

**Frontend** — add the two optional fields to the `s3` entry in
[connectionFormSpec.ts:91](frontend/src/components/connections/connectionFormSpec.ts#L91),
following the existing optional-field pattern. No new connection type, so the ~20
type-registration points (`check_service`, `run_target`, `dataset_reader`,
`profile_service`, `schema_drift`, `asset_identity`, `connections.ts`, …) are untouched.

**Security note for the PR:** an operator-supplied endpoint is a fetch target
(SSRF-shaped). This matches the existing posture for `adls_gen2.account_url` and
`iceberg.catalog_uri` — connection configs are admin-authored — and the scheme is
validated. Call it out explicitly in the PR rather than letting it pass unexamined.

**Tests** (`backend/tests/datasources/test_s3.py`, `test_flatfile.py`, dbt tests):
config validation incl. `auto → path` inference and scheme rejection; assert the boto3
kwargs actually carry `endpoint_url` and `s3={"addressing_style": ...}`. Per the
standing habit, **mutation-check each new regression test** — revert the fix and confirm
it fails for the right reason.

---

## Part 1 — Harness: local Airflow mirroring Container Apps

`~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/local/docker-compose.yml`, same topology as
`terraform/airflow.tf`: postgres (metadata) · redis (broker) · `airflow-init` (db migrate
+ admin user) · scheduler · webserver · celery worker — all from the **existing**
`airflow/Dockerfile` (`apache/airflow:2.10.5` + DAGs + client libs), CeleryExecutor,
reusing the env var names from `local.airflow_env` verbatim
(`EXECUTE_TASKS_NEW_PYTHON_INTERPRETER`, `LOAD_EXAMPLES=False`,
`API__AUTH_BACKENDS=basic_auth,session`).

**One blocker to fix in the image:** `airflow/webserver_config.py` reads
`os.environ["AZURE_OAUTH_TENANT_ID"]` at import and hard-`KeyError`s without Entra vars —
and the init container imports it too. Make it fall back to `AUTH_DB` when the OAuth env
is absent, so **one image** serves both ACA (Entra SSO) and local (basic auth). The REST
basic-auth path DataQ polls stays identical either way.

**MinIO** service + an `mc` bootstrap container creating the `landing` bucket and an
access key.

**Networking:** declare DataQ's compose network as `external` so DataQ's api/worker reach
`http://airflow-webserver:8080` and the DAG callback reaches
`http://api:8000/api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow`. The DataQ Airflow connection's
`base_url` **must equal** `DATAQ_AIRFLOW_BASE_URL` — run attribution depends on it.

**`local/harness_local.sh`** — the `scripts/harness_window.sh` analogue:
`up | seed | run [--dags] | down`, driving the same DAG list over the Airflow REST API.

---

## Part 2 — Harness writers move to S3

- **`mockdata/storage.py`** — add `S3Store` beside `LocalStore`/`AdlsStore` and teach
  `make_store` the `s3://<bucket>/<prefix>` scheme. ~30 lines, mirrors `AdlsStore`.
- **`airflow/dags/_harness.py`** — `_adls_filesystem` / `count_feed_files` / `read_feed`
  are DataLake-only; add an S3 path selected by env so the **same DAG files** run in both
  places, unedited.
- **Event modality (bonus of choosing S3):** MinIO bucket notifications can POST to a
  webhook on `s3:ObjectCreated`. Reuse the `eventgrid_receiver/` shape to translate that
  into `POST /api/v1/dags/flow_a_payments_event/dagRuns`, preserving the event-driven
  Airflow row of the orchestration matrix locally. Azurite has no equivalent.

---

## Part 3 — Staged: local Iceberg targets (no DataQ code)

Verified above: `catalog_type=sql` + a SQLite catalog URI + a local or MinIO warehouse
(`properties={"s3.endpoint": ...}`) already works, credential-less. Add DAG variants that
write Iceberg instead of Snowflake/UC so the stack survives those accounts lapsing. Flow
D's `iceberg-writer` is the working precedent. Sequenced after Parts 0–2 land and are
proven.

---

## Part 4 — Docs

- `docs/datasources-checks.md` + `docs/feature-matrix.md` — S3-compatible endpoints.
- `docs/ops-log.md` — the readiness exercise, and the ADF contingency: Azure-only SaaS,
  no emulator, so on a real wind-down the provider keeps its code/tests/docs but loses
  live coverage. Recorded, not actioned.
- Harness `README.md` — the local section + the MinIO/AGPL boundary.

No new ADR: ADR 0021 already covers the harness, and `endpoint_url` is a config
extension, not an architecture decision.

---

## Verification

**Gate before push** (local, not CI-first): Black · Ruff · mypy · **Bandit** · pytest with
the `--cov-fail-under=80` gate · frontend lint/test. Then `/code-review` agents on the PR.

**Live proof — the point of the exercise.** Fixtures cannot settle this: MinIO is a
different server implementation from AWS, and `LastModified` / `head_object` /
`list_objects_v2` cross a driver boundary. Only a live run is evidence (the UC-freshness
and Parquet-freshness lesson).

1. Bring up the local stack; seed via `mockdata` → MinIO.
2. Create a DataQ `s3` connection with `endpoint_url` pointing at MinIO → **Test** green.
3. Run the flat-file suite → rows read; run **volume** and **arrival-time freshness**
   monitors and confirm real readings off MinIO's `LastModified`.
4. Trigger a DAG over the Airflow REST API; confirm DataQ records the `pipeline_run`
   **both** via 10-min polling **and** via the HMAC callback, and that a bound suite fires.
5. Confirm the dbt artifact poller reads `run_results.json` from MinIO.
6. Re-run the same S3 checks against real AWS (or the existing suites) to prove the
   `auto` addressing default did not regress the AWS path.

**PRs:** (1) S3-compatible endpoints + tests, (2) docs. The harness is untracked — no PR.

gh issue create --title "S3 connection: support S3-compatible endpoints (endpoint_url + addressing style)" --label "enhancement,priority/P2" --milestone "v1.1 Week 5 — anomaly monitor kind + metric trends" --body 'The `s3` datasource connection can only ever address **AWS S3**. `S3Config` has no endpoint field, so `boto3.client("s3", ...)` always resolves the AWS regional endpoint — there is no way to point DataQ at MinIO, Ceph/RadosGW, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, Backblaze B2, SeaweedFS, or a corporate on-prem object store, all of which speak the S3 API.

This is a real product gap (S3-compatible storage is common in on-prem and cost-sensitive deployments), and it is also what a fully local, Azure-free harness needs for its flat-file landing zone.

## Scope

Add two optional, non-secret fields to the S3 connection config:

- `endpoint_url: str | None` — validated `http(s)://`, trailing slash stripped (mirroring `AdlsConfig._http_url` in `backend/app/datasources/adls.py`).
- `addressing_style: "auto" | "path" | "virtual"`, default `auto` → **path** when `endpoint_url` is set, boto3 default otherwise.

The addressing style is **not** optional polish: MinIO and SeaweedFS reject virtual-host addressing, so without it boto3 resolves `<bucket>.<host>` and every request fails. Defaulting to `auto` keeps the existing AWS behaviour byte-identical when no endpoint is configured.

## Where it lands

Three boto3 client construction sites, all of which already receive the config:

- `backend/app/datasources/s3.py` — `S3Config` + `S3ConnectionAdapter.test`.
- `backend/app/datasources/flatfile.py` — `_s3_client`, the single factory behind `download_bytes`, `object_size`, `read_range`, `iter_files` and the schema/count reads. One change covers every flat-file read path.
- `backend/app/orchestration/dbt.py` — `DbtConfig` + the `s3` branch of `_read_artifact`. Included deliberately: leaving it out would make the dbt artifact poller the one S3 path that cannot reach an S3-compatible store, and two S3 clients quietly diverging is the kind of drift this codebase avoids.

Plus the optional fields on the `s3` entry in `frontend/src/components/connections/connectionFormSpec.ts`, and `docs/datasources-checks.md` / `docs/feature-matrix.md`.

No new connection type, so none of the ~20 type-registration points (`check_service`, `run_target`, `dataset_reader`, `profile_service`, `schema_drift`, `asset_identity`, `connections.ts`, …) are touched.

## Security note

An operator-supplied endpoint is a fetch target (SSRF-shaped). This matches the existing posture for `adls_gen2.account_url` and `iceberg.catalog_uri` — connection configs are admin-authored — and the scheme is validated. Recording it here so the consideration is examined rather than implicit.

## Verification

Unit tests cannot settle this alone: a non-AWS S3 server is a different implementation, and `LastModified` / `head_object` / `list_objects_v2` cross a driver boundary (the UC-freshness and Parquet-freshness lesson). Acceptance requires a **live run** against a real S3-compatible server — connection test green, a flat-file suite reading rows, and volume + arrival-time freshness monitors returning real readings — plus a re-run against AWS S3 to prove the `auto` default did not regress the existing path.'

"""S3 connection adapter — AWS S3 and any S3-compatible store.

"""S3-compatible endpoint configuration, shared by every S3 client DataQ builds.

Three places construct a boto3 S3 client — the S3 datasource adapter
(`datasources/s3.py`), the flat-file read paths (`datasources/flatfile.py`) and
the dbt artifacts poll (`orchestration/dbt.py`) — and a store is only usable if
all of them agree on how to reach it. This module owns that one decision, exactly
as `core/credential_expiry.py` owns credential lifetime for both a datasource
adapter and an orchestration provider.

**Why an endpoint at all (#1063).** MinIO, Ceph/RadosGW, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi,
Backblaze B2, SeaweedFS and on-prem gateways all speak the S3 API; boto3 reaches
any of them by endpoint. Unset, every client resolves the AWS regional endpoint
exactly as it did before — the AWS path is deliberately left byte-identical.
"""

#: ``<bucket>.<host>/<key>``) or in the path (``path``, ``<host>/<bucket>/<key>``).
#: ``auto`` is DataQ's inference, not botocore's — see `resolve_addressing_style`.
S3AddressingStyle = Literal["auto", "path", "virtual"]


def normalize_endpoint_url(value: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Validate + tidy an S3-compatible endpoint; ``None``/blank means AWS.

    Shared by `S3Config` and `DbtConfig` so an endpoint is accepted in exactly one
    shape wherever it is configured. Mirrors `AdlsConfig._http_url`: the scheme is
    checked here rather than left to boto3, which would otherwise accept
    ``minio:9000`` and fail later with a connection error that says nothing about
    the missing scheme.
    """
    if value is None:
        return None
    stripped = value.strip()
    if not stripped:
        return None
    if not stripped.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        raise ValueError("endpoint_url must start with http:// or https://")
    return stripped.rstrip("/")


def resolve_addressing_style(
    endpoint_url: str | None, addressing_style: S3AddressingStyle
) -> str | None:
    """The botocore ``s3.addressing_style``, or ``None`` to leave boto3's default.

    ``auto`` resolves to **path** whenever an endpoint is set. This is load-bearing,
    not a nicety: MinIO and SeaweedFS serve the bucket in the path only, so under
    boto3's default (virtual-host) addressing the client resolves
    ``<bucket>.<host>`` — a name that does not exist — and *every* request fails.
    AWS is unaffected because ``auto`` without an endpoint returns ``None`` here,
    leaving the client constructed exactly as it was before #1063.

    An operator who needs the other behaviour (R2 and Wasabi accept virtual-host;
    a path-style-only proxy in front of AWS is also real) sets ``path``/``virtual``
    explicitly and this passes it straight through.
    """
    if addressing_style != "auto":
        return addressing_style
    return "path" if endpoint_url else None


def addressing_config_kwargs(
    endpoint_url: str | None, addressing_style: S3AddressingStyle
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Extra ``botocore.config.Config`` kwargs; ``{}`` leaves the default untouched.

    Each of the three client sites owns its own timeouts and retry policy, so this
    returns the addressing fragment to splat into that site's `Config` rather than
    a whole `Config` — one shared decision, three different transport policies.
    """

def normalize_addressing_style(value: Any) -> Any:
    """Treat a blank addressing style as unset, i.e. ``auto``.

    A ``mode="before"`` coercion, because the field is a `Literal` and ``""``
    would be rejected by it. Blank genuinely reaches here: the connection form
    renders this as an optional text input, so a user who types and then clears it
    submits ``""`` rather than omitting the key — and the same shape arrives from
    the public API and from a suite export/import round-trip. "Left blank" means
    "no preference", which is exactly ``auto``.

    Anything else passes through untouched so a genuine typo still fails loudly
    against the `Literal` rather than being silently coerced to a default.
    """
    if isinstance(value, str) and not value.strip():
        return "auto"
    return value

content.text: While writing the docs I found a real consequence of this change that must not ship silently:

input.command:
gh issue create --title "S3 asset identity collides across endpoints once S3-compatible stores are supported" --label "bug,priority/P2" --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" --body 'Found while implementing #1063 (S3-compatible endpoints). Filing rather than fixing inside that PR: the fix changes an **asset namespace**, which is a persisted identity that lineage, incidents and scorecards hang off, so the convention deserves its own decision rather than riding along.

## The defect

`_resolve_s3` in `backend/app/services/asset_identity.py` derives the asset namespace from the bucket alone:

```python
namespace = f"s3://{bucket}"
```

That was **sound before #1063**, because every `s3` connection was AWS and AWS bucket names are globally unique — the bucket *was* a global identity.

Once a connection can carry an `endpoint_url`, bucket names are only unique **within an endpoint**. Two different stores with the same bucket name now resolve to the same `AssetIdentity`:

- AWS bucket `landing` → `s3://landing`
- MinIO at `https://minio.internal:9000`, bucket `landing` → `s3://landing`

## Failure scenario

An operator monitors an AWS bucket `analytics` and an on-prem MinIO bucket also named `analytics`. Both connections resolve to the asset `s3://analytics`, so DataQ merges them into **one** asset row. The consequences are all silent:

- the asset scorecard aggregates checks from two unrelated datasets into one score;
- lineage edges from both stores land on the same node, producing a graph that shows a dependency that does not exist;
- an incident raised on one store is attributed to the asset the other store also owns.

Nothing errors — the platform simply reports confidently about a dataset that is two datasets.

## Constraints on the fix

- **The AWS namespace must not change.** `s3://{bucket}` is the OpenLineage naming-spec form for AWS and is already persisted on `assets` rows in production; changing it would fork every existing S3 asset and orphan its lineage and incidents — the stability property `_resolve_iceberg` documents in the same module.
- So the endpoint host should only participate when `endpoint_url` is **set**, which is also why fixing it early is cheap: no S3-compatible connection exists yet, so there is nothing to migrate today. That window closes as soon as anyone creates one.
- The convention needs picking deliberately (OpenLineage does not standardise the S3-compatible case; candidates include folding the endpoint host/port into the namespace).

## Scope

- `backend/app/services/asset_identity.py::_resolve_s3`
- a test asserting that two connections with the same bucket and **different** endpoints resolve to different identities, and that an endpoint-less AWS connection still resolves to exactly `s3://{bucket}`.'

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(datasources): address any S3-compatible store, not just AWS

The `s3` connection could only ever reach AWS: no endpoint field existed, so
every boto3 client resolved the AWS regional endpoint. That ruled out MinIO,
Ceph/RadosGW, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, Backblaze B2, SeaweedFS and on-prem
gateways — all of which speak the S3 API — and it is also what a fully local,
Azure-free harness needs for its flat-file landing zone.

Adds two optional non-secret config fields, `endpoint_url` and
`addressing_style`, resolved by one shared helper (`core/s3_endpoint.py`) so
that all three places DataQ builds an S3 client agree on how to reach a store:
the connection probe (`datasources/s3.py`), every flat-file read path
(`datasources/flatfile.py::_s3_client`) and the dbt artifacts poll
(`orchestration/dbt.py`). The dbt half is deliberate — left out, the poller
would be the one S3 path pinned to AWS, so a dbt project whose artifacts sit
beside its data would look configured and silently never poll.

`addressing_style` defaults to `auto`, which means **path** whenever an endpoint
is set. That is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: MinIO and SeaweedFS serve the
bucket in the path only, so under boto3's virtual-host default the client
resolves `<bucket>.<host>` and every request fails. With no endpoint, `auto`
returns None and the AWS client is constructed exactly as before — asserted
directly against a real boto3 client, not a recorded kwarg, so the guard proves
what botocore resolved rather than what we passed.

Blank values coerce to "unset" (`endpoint_url` -> None, `addressing_style` ->
auto) because the connection form submits "" for an optional field a user typed
into and then cleared, and the same shape arrives from the public API and from
an export/import round-trip; a genuine typo still fails loudly against the
Literal.

Filed #1064: `_resolve_s3` derives an asset namespace from the bucket alone,
which was sound while every connection was AWS (globally unique bucket names)
but collides once two stores can share a bucket name.

Fixes #1063

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

## What

The `s3` connection could only ever reach **AWS**: `S3Config` had no endpoint field, so every boto3 client resolved the AWS regional endpoint. This adds two optional non-secret config fields — `endpoint_url` and `addressing_style` — so the same connection, checks and monitors work against MinIO, Ceph/RadosGW, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, Backblaze B2, SeaweedFS or an on-prem gateway.

It also unblocks a fully local, Azure-free harness for the flat-file landing zone.

## Where

One shared helper, `backend/app/core/s3_endpoint.py`, owns the endpoint + addressing decision — the `core/credential_expiry.py` pattern, which is likewise imported by both a datasource adapter and an orchestration provider. All three places DataQ builds an S3 client consume it:

| Site | Covers |
|---|---|
| `datasources/s3.py` | the connection `test()` probe |
| `datasources/flatfile.py::_s3_client` | every read path — `download_bytes`, `object_size`, `read_range`, `iter_files`, schema/count |
| `orchestration/dbt.py::_read_artifact` | the dbt artifacts poll |

**The dbt half is deliberate.** Left out, the poller would be the one S3 path pinned to AWS, so a dbt project whose artifacts sit beside its data in a compatible store would look configured and silently never poll — the connection would simply report no runs.

## Two decisions worth reviewing

**1. `auto` means path addressing whenever an endpoint is set.** This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: MinIO and SeaweedFS serve the bucket in the path only, so under boto3'"'"'s virtual-host default the client resolves `<bucket>.<host>` — a host that does not exist — and *every* request fails with what looks like a network fault. With no endpoint, `auto` returns `None` and the client is built exactly as before.

**2. Blank coerces to unset** (`endpoint_url` → `None`, `addressing_style` → `auto`). The connection form renders these as optional text inputs, so a user who types into one and then clears it submits `""`, not an absent key — and the same shape arrives from the public API and from an export/import round-trip. `endpoint_url=""` would be a real-and-broken endpoint to boto3, and `addressing_style=""` would be rejected by the `Literal`. A genuine typo (`"pth"`) still fails loudly.

## Tests

`backend/tests/core/test_s3_endpoint.py` (new) asserts the rules once; each client site then asserts it applies them.

The flat-file guards construct a **real boto3 client** and assert `client.meta.endpoint_url` / `client.meta.config.s3` rather than a recorded kwarg — the question that matters is what botocore *resolved*, not what we passed. That includes an explicit AWS regression guard (`https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com`, `config.s3 is None`), so if `auto` ever started pinning a style unconditionally, existing AWS connections would fail the build.

Every new regression test was **mutation-checked** — reverted against three separate mutants (auto never infers path; `endpoint_url` dropped before boto3; blank coercion removed) and each failed for its own reason:

```
mutant 1 (auto never resolves to path)  -> 5 failures, one at each client site
mutant 2 (endpoint dropped in flatfile) -> test_s3_client_resolves_a_compatible_endpoint
mutant 3 (blank coercion removed)       -> the 3 blank-coercion tests
```

## Filed, not fixed here

**#1064** — `asset_identity._resolve_s3` derives the asset namespace from the bucket alone (`s3://{bucket}`). That was sound while every `s3` connection was AWS, where bucket names are globally unique; once two stores can share a bucket name, an AWS `analytics` bucket and an on-prem MinIO `analytics` bucket merge into one asset, silently combining scorecards, lineage and incidents. Filed separately because the fix changes a **persisted** asset namespace, and the AWS form must not change (it would fork every existing S3 asset), so the convention deserves its own decision.

## Security

An operator-supplied endpoint is a fetch target (SSRF-shaped). This matches the existing posture for `adls_gen2.account_url` and `iceberg.catalog_uri` — connection configs are admin-authored — and the scheme is validated at save time rather than left to boto3. Recording it explicitly so it is examined rather than implicit.

## Verification

- Local gate green: Black · Ruff · mypy (`backend/app` + `backend/tests`) · Bandit · **2864 backend tests, 97.21% coverage** · frontend lint/format + **671 tests**.
- ⚠️ **Live proof against a real S3-compatible server is still outstanding** and is the acceptance bar for this feature — unit tests cannot settle it, because a non-AWS server is a different implementation and `LastModified` / `head_object` / `list_objects_v2` cross a driver boundary (the UC-freshness and Parquet-freshness lesson). Planned as part of the local-harness work that motivated this: connection test green, a flat-file suite reading rows, and volume + arrival-time freshness returning real readings off MinIO.

class S3Store(Store):
    """S3 store — AWS or any S3-compatible server (MinIO in the local stack).

    The Azure-free sibling of `AdlsStore`, so the same generator feeds either
    landing zone unchanged. Auth + endpoint come from the standard boto3 env
    (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`) plus
    `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` for a compatible server.

    Path addressing is forced whenever an endpoint is set — MinIO serves the
    bucket in the path only, and under boto3's virtual-host default every request
    would resolve `<bucket>.<host>` and fail. Same rule DataQ applies in
    `core/s3_endpoint.py`; the two must agree or the writer and the reader
    disagree about where a file is.

    boto3 is lazy-imported (like the azure libs above) so local-store runs work
    without it installed.
    """

    def __init__(self, bucket: str, prefix: str) -> None:
        import os

        import boto3
        from botocore.config import Config
        from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

        self._ClientError = ClientError
        self.bucket = bucket
        self.prefix = prefix.strip("/")
        endpoint = os.environ.get("AWS_ENDPOINT_URL") or None
        self._s3 = boto3.client(
            "s3",
            endpoint_url=endpoint,
            config=Config(s3={"addressing_style": "path"}) if endpoint else None,
        )

    def _key(self, rel: str) -> str:
        return f"{self.prefix}/{rel}" if self.prefix else rel

    def exists(self, rel: str) -> bool:
        try:
            self._s3.head_object(Bucket=self.bucket, Key=self._key(rel))
            return True
        except self._ClientError as exc:
            # Only "it isn't there" is a False; anything else (403, throttling, a
            # broken endpoint) must propagate rather than be reported as absence —
            # a state file silently read as missing restarts the feed from zero.
            if exc.response.get("Error", {}).get("Code") in ("404", "NoSuchKey", "NotFound"):
                return False
            raise

    def read_bytes(self, rel: str) -> bytes:
        body: bytes = self._s3.get_object(Bucket=self.bucket, Key=self._key(rel))["Body"].read()
        return body

    def write_bytes(self, rel: str, data: bytes) -> None:
        self._s3.put_object(Bucket=self.bucket, Key=self._key(rel), Body=data)


def make_store(uri: str) -> Store:
    """`adls://<acct>/<fs>/<prefix>` -> ADLS, `s3://<bucket>/<prefix>` -> S3,
    anything else -> local path."""
    if uri.startswith("adls://"):
        parts = uri[len("adls://") :].split("/", 2)
        if len(parts) < 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"bad adls uri {uri!r}; expected adls://<account>/<filesystem>[/<prefix>]"
            )
        account, filesystem = parts[0], parts[1]
        prefix = parts[2] if len(parts) == 3 else ""
        return AdlsStore(account, filesystem, prefix)
    if uri.startswith("s3://"):
        bucket, _, prefix = uri[len("s3://") :].partition("/")
        if not bucket:
            raise ValueError(f"bad s3 uri {uri!r}; expected s3://<bucket>[/<prefix>]")
        return S3Store(bucket, prefix)
    return LocalStore(uri)
